SEEBITS

Inspect your 3D-print model at true size — in 2D and in VR

See the bits of your model — inspect 3D-print files, STL or GLB, at true size, in 2D or VR. Free, no install, no account. Your files never leave your device.

START WITH YOUR FILE

…or drop files anywhere on this page.

Several files load together as one assembly; an STL with several shells splits into parts automatically. .stl and .glb only — a .gltf needing separate files can't load, and a .3mf won't open.

On a headset? Pick your file in the 2D panel before tapping Enter VR — files can't be picked inside VR.

VR HEIGHT — SEATED OR STANDING

Seated (default) ≈ 1.0 m · Standing ≈ 1.35 m — the model's centre height in VR.

ON A QUEST HEADSET — YOUR FILE, STEP BY STEP

  1. Get the file into the headset's Downloads — via Quest Browser, the Files app (Google Drive), or USB into the Download folder.
  2. Hold the Meta button → apps grid → Browser (globe icon) → caitriaoneill.com/vr. Stay in the flat 2D panel.
  3. Tap Choose your file above; in the picker, go to Downloads and pick your STL or GLB.
  4. Check the model is on screen, then tap 🥽 Enter VR in the bottom bar.

Known snag: a Quest Browser bug can refuse a picked file (access-denied; reported for .glb). If that happens, it's the bug, not your file — the built-ins below always work, or load the file on phone/desktop first.

OR OPEN A BUILT-IN MODEL

No file needed. The demo is the MidiBitty — a real printed case, already assembled.

CONTROLS — THE SHORT LIST

  • Drag to orbit · scroll or pinch to zoom · tap a part to select it.
  • Apart slider (bottom bar) pulls an assembly apart so you can see inside it.
  • ☰ Tools: Parts, Measure & Fit, Look. Tap a part for its colour and finish. ↺ Reset restores the model exactly as it loaded.
  • In VR: panels beside you. Apart, ⇄ Mode and ↺ Reset float by the model's base. A quick pinch in empty air hides or returns the panels; EXIT VR is on the right panel. Pinch-and-hold a part to grab it.

Reopen any time with Start here / Help (bottom bar).

Controls

The same model, three ways to hold it.

PHONE & DESKTOP

DragOrbit around the model
Pinch / scrollZoom
Two-finger drag / right-dragPan
Tap / click a partSelect it (highlight + name + a soft click)
Apart slider + directionFans parts out into a separated stack. Vertical (the default): up the assembly axis. Horizontal: along the longest axis. Mixed: both. Needs more than one part — a single solid has nothing to separate
Section sliderSlice the model open with a clipping plane
MeasureTap two points — distance in mm. Label what you measured (Gap / Hole / Peg / Wall) in the result bar; the fit verdict uses the band for that feature and your material
MidiBitty — the DemoThe ⟡ Demo button (Tools, landing, VR panel) loads the MidiBitty v0.7 case: six files, shells split into 19 parts — no upload needed, so it's the reliable headset route. Also loads from ?sample=midibitty
Colour & finish (selected part)Tap a part: the selected-part bar carries colour swatches, a custom picker, and a finish (gloss, matte, or translucent). Applies live; saved per part name. In VR, the panel's Colour / Finish buttons cycle the same presets
Built-in models dropdownFour built-ins, in Tools, the landing and the empty state: MidiBitty — Demo (6-file case), Planetary gear set, Geneva drive (both generated in the page), Cosmic Buddha (Smithsonian, CC0, ~1.51 m, single piece). Each also loads via ?model=
Inspector (keys 1–5, or I)Shaded · MatCap · Normals · Wireframe overlay · Flat — the Sketchfab Inspector idea, adapted
Stats + Print CheckIn Tools → Measure & Fit: dimensions, triangles, volume, surface area, a manifold check (skipped above 500,000 triangles), and pointers from this model and your printer/material

IN THE HEADSET (QUEST) — HANDS FIRST

Pinch on a partTap to select it — a quick pinch is a tap. With controllers, this is the trigger.
Load a built-in in VRThe panel's LOAD rows load the same four built-ins as the flat page — no upload needed; the model lands centred in front of you
Reset — back to as loaded↺ Reset (bottom bar, Tools, VR panel, floating Reset pill) returns everything to how it was when the file loaded: part positions and rotations, Apart 0%, section cut cleared, hidden/ghosted parts restored, colours and finishes, grabs undone, view restored
Grab mode — Single part / Whole modelIn Tools (Parts) and on the VR panel: Single part — tap selects one component, pinch-hold moves only it. Whole model — tap selects everything, pinch-hold carries all parts as one model, so a grab can't pull a layer out
Ghost handsYour hands render as a faint ghost — joint dots and bone lines, theme-tinted — alongside the pointer ray. They never cover the model
Glow particles stay out of your sightlineGalaxy's ambient glow particles are kept out of the corridor between your face and the model or panel, and never within ~30 cm of your face. The geometry is in Scenes — how they're built, below
Two scenes — Cyber and GalaxyCyber: an empty Tron void — grid floor, horizon ring, platform. Galaxy: cosmos only — night sky, ringed planet, orbiting moon; no ground, no shelf, so nothing can hide the model. Different constructions, not a recolour
Pinch on a part and hold, then dragGrab that part: drag moves it, twisting your wrist rotates it; release to let go. With controllers, grip on a part does the same grab
Grip, empty air (controllers)Grab the world and pull it around you (controllers only). With hands, recover the model's position with the floating Reset pill or the panel's Reset model. The world is clamped near home, so it can't be thrown out of reach
Scene switchThe Cyber | Galaxy segments in the bottom bar beside Apart (filled side = the scene you're in), and the floating Mode pill in VR. The choice persists between visits
Galaxy sparklesGalaxy only (Cyber has none): the sky drifts and twinkles, a glow field surrounds the model. The grab trail and print-check shooting star have their own rows below. Sparkles never touch the model, measurements or warnings
Print check passesIn Galaxy, a pass — and only a pass — earns one shooting star plus a sparkle ring around the model. A flagged check gets nothing
Fingertip glow trailIn Galaxy, while a one-hand pinch-grab is active a trail of soft glows follows your pinch point — visible grab confirmation, since hand tracking has no haptics. It stops the moment you release
Show all (Tools / VR panels)Restores every part to shown with its chosen appearance kept (a translucent part comes back translucent), makes every mesh visible, and clears any section cut
Floating Apart, Mode + ResetThree controls float in space, visible all session: the Apart pill is the slider — pinch-hold and drag (0 re-assembles); the Mode pill switches scene, even with panels hidden; the ↺ Reset pill restores the model as loaded
Two hands pinch-hold the modelMove both hands to carry the target; spread or close them to scale; swing the line between them to turn and tilt. Starts only when both hands pinch-hold the model. Reset undoes it, scale included
Drag a panel / floating control by its dotted gripPinch-hold the dotted grip on a panel header or pill and move your hand: the surface follows, facing you, and stays where dropped — clamped within reach. Dragging starts only on the grip, so it never presses a button underneath
Nothing the model sits on can block your viewThe surfaces under the model (Cyber platform, bench grid, shadow catcher; Galaxy has none) fade transparent whenever they'd cross your sightline, or your viewpoint drops below the model's base plane — you can look up through where the model sits
BRING UP / PUT AWAY THE PANELS — quick pinch in empty airParts & Layers at your left, Tools & Settings at your right. A quick pinch in empty air hides both panels; pinch again to bring them back — a lost panel is re-placed instead. Resize by pinching a corner bracket
Quick pinch (either hand) — detailsSummon / dismiss uses a quick pinch only — a held pinch is left to the system (see Leave VR / AR). If the model seems missing, a summoning pinch also retries placing it in front of you
Panel buttonsContextual only. Left panel: part groups, selected part. Right panel: LOAD, grab target, Apart, selected part (state, Colour / Finish), Show all, Reset, EXIT VR. View modes, Apart direction, units and Measure & Fit are set on the flat page
Thumbstick flick (controllers)Snap-turn 30° (sticks never scroll the explode). No hands equivalent — turning your body does the same thing.
Leave VR / ARPinch EXIT VR on the right panel — panels hidden? One quick pinch in empty air brings them back. Left palm: pinch-and-hold the Meta icon for system menu. Controllers: B (right) / Y (left), or Meta → Quit

THE PIPELINE

1 · IdeaSketch it, measure the real thing it must fit
2 · OpenSCADDescribe the shape in code; every dimension is a number you can change
3 · STLExport one STL per part, in assembled coordinates
4 · VRLoad the STLs here — check fit and scale at true 1:1 before anything prints

Formats: GLB keeps part names — it carries its parts' names and structure. STL carries no names, so its parts are named after their files. A .gltf referencing separate .bin or texture files isn't supported — export a single .glb.

SCENES — HOW THEY'RE BUILT

The two scenes are different constructions. Cyber is a handful of draw calls: a grid floor, a horizon ring, a platform — an empty Tron void. Galaxy is the all-out scene: one shader sky shell + twinkling star shells + celestial bodies + fake glow — no bloom, no post-processing, no real reflections, so it stays smooth on Quest. The sky's nebula is LYGIA fbm, domain-warped the Shadertoy way: the noise domain is warped by fbm itself, density shaped with a power curve, colour through LYGIA's cosine palette (octaves held to 3 for Quest). The same fbm breaks up the aurora curtains; the same palette cycles the arch crystal's iridescence. Glow is emissive cores plus soft halo sprites; bench shine is an environment map plus a fresnel sheen, never a second render.

Cyber: near-black void, a cyan grid floor running to a glowing horizon ring, and a low platform with a light ring under the model. Nothing else — no sky, no landmarks, no particles. Galaxy: the Milky Way band arcing behind the arch, layered nebula sprites, thousands of tiny soft-glow stars in layered shells at different depths (radial-gradient sprites, not square points), a slowly drifting ringed planet with an orbiting moon, and two companion bodies — shader-lit with a fixed sun and a light floor in their own shader, so a body can never render as a black void. Galaxy is cosmos only — no ground, no terrace, no shelf.

Why Galaxy has no ground: an opaque shelf under the model hid grabbed parts and flickered, so the terrace, mountains and ground apron are gone. The dark mid-field arch, shards and rocks went too — parented to the model group, they swung around as near-black shapes when the model was grabbed. Nothing dark sits in the mid-field, so nothing can hide a part at any position.

Your sightline rule is geometry, not a hope: ambient motes live only in a lateral ring (azimuth ±40° to ±170° from forward, 2.5–12 m out) or the far sky (beyond 30 m) — never in the corridor between your face and the model or panel, and never within 1.2 m of your head. Their orbits are computed in the vertex shader from per-point attributes, checked against that corridor when placed, so nothing can wander into your view. A comet / satellite pass crosses only the far sky, high up, with long gaps.

Budget, honestly: the environment is capped at roughly 45 draw calls of a total target under 100, leaving the rest for your model and the UI. These are documented Quest budgets (72 fps = 13.9 ms per frame, everything drawn twice, once per eye), not measurements taken on your headset — your retest in the headset is still the real measurement, especially for nebula-sprite overdraw in stereo.

Licence boundary: LYGIA's Prosperity terms and Shadertoy's CC BY-NC-SA both bar commercial use, so if this viewer ever went commercial those two forks would need a commercial licence (LYGIA Patron) or removal — for this non-commercial project they are in terms as-is. A source's own explicit prohibitions still bind; nothing here overrides them.

Open questions, plainly: no live Quest rendering was performed for the research behind these scenes, so the performance figures above are documented budgets, not measurements of this viewer. Solar System Scope's current terms were reported as CC BY 4.0 by secondary sources (older sources said non-commercial only) — another reason this build draws the planet procedurally and ships no downloaded texture at all.
